etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English corage, from Old French corage (French courage), from Vulgar Latin *corāticum, from Latin cor (“heart”). Distantly related to cardiac (“of the heart”), which is from Greek, but from the same Proto-Indo-European root. Displaced Middle English elne, ellen, from Old English ellen (“courage, valor”).

definitions.definition: The quality of being confident, not afraid or easily intimidated, but without being incautious or inconsiderate.

quote.citation: 1860, R[alph] W[aldo] Emerson, “Essay IV. Culture.”, in The Conduct of Life, Boston, Mass.: Ticknor and Fields, →OCLC, page 120:
quote.text: A great part of courage is the courage of having done the thing before.

quote.citation: 1813 January 27, [Jane Austen], Pride and Prejudice: […], volume (please specify |volume=I to III), London:  […]  [George Sidney] for T[homas] Egerton, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others. My courage always rises at every attempt to intimidate me.

definitions.definition: The ability to overcome one's fear, do or live things which one finds frightening.

quote.citation: 1897, Mark Twain [pseudonym; Samuel Langhorne Clemens], “[Pudd’nhead Wilson] Chapter XII”, in The Tragedy of Pudd’nhead Wilson: And the Comedy Those Extraordinary Twins, Hartford, Conn.: American Publishing Company, →OCLC, page 155:
quote.text: Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear—not absence of fear.

definitions.definition: The ability to maintain one's will or intent despite either the experience of fear, frailty, or frustration; or the occurrence of adversity, difficulty, defeat or reversal.  Moral fortitude.

quote.text: “Courage is not simply one of the virtues but the form of every virtue at the testing point, which means at the point of highest reality.”

quote.citation: 1960 July 11, Harper Lee, To Kill a Mockingbird, Philadelphia, Pa., New York, N.Y.: J[oshua] B[allinger] Lippincott Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: I wanted you to see what real courage is, instead of getting the idea that courage is a man with a gun in his hand. It's when you know you're licked before you begin, but you begin anyway and see it through no matter what.

quote.citation: 1993, Stanley P. Cornils, The Mourning After: How to Manage Grief Wisely:
quote.text: Courage isn't having the strength to go on - it is going on when you don't have strength.

quote.citation: 2008, Maya Angelou, address for the 2008 Cornell University commencement
quote.text: Courage is the most important of all the virtues because without courage, you can't practice any other virtue consistently.

quote.citation: 2008, Eric Roth, The Curious Case of Benjamin Button Screenplay:
quote.text: I hope you live a life you’re proud of. If you find that you’re not, I hope you have the courage to start all over again.

quote.citation: 1485, Sir Thomas Malory, chapter X, in Le Morte Darthur, book XIX:
quote.text: And wete yow wel sayd kynge Arthur vnto Vrres syster I shalle begynne to handle hym and serche vnto my power not presumyng vpon me that I am soo worthy to hele youre sone by my dedes / but I wille courage other men of worshyp to doo as I wylle doo(please add an English translation of this quotation)

quote.citation: 1530, William Tyndale, An Answer unto Sir Thomas More's Dialogue:
quote.text: Paul writeth unto Timothy, to instruct him, to teach him, to exhort, to courage him, to stir him up,
